worked-example.title: Worked example: a spam filter and Bayes' theorem

sections.heading: The exercise
sections.markdown: 30% of emails are spam. The word "winner" appears in 40% of spam and in 2% of regular email. An email contains the word. What is the probability that it is spam?

sections.heading: Hint 1
sections.markdown: Let $S$=spam and $W$=the word appears. What are you asked for: $P(S\mid W)$ or $P(W\mid S)$?

sections.heading: Hint 2
sections.markdown: Compute $P(W)$ with the law of total probability over the partition $\{S, S^c\}$.

sections.heading: Sanity check
sections.markdown: The result is higher than 0.3 (the word raises the suspicion) and lower than 1 — it makes sense.
